known_differences_from_fetch_script: Step order differs: the script filters offense, then coordinates, then year, then de-duplicates (01_fetch_buffalo.py:182-205); the runner applies year, id, offense, coordinates, de-duplication. No effect on raw_cache.parquet: case_number has 92,274 distinct values in 92,274 rows (evidence/raw_cache_profile.json, case_number.distinct_count), so de-duplication drops nothing in either order and the other filters are row-wise and commute.

Non-numeric coordinates: the script coerces latitude/longitude with pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce') (01_fetch_buffalo.py:189-190), turning the 2,893 'UNKNOWN' strings (evidence/raw_cache_profile.json, latitude/longitude distinct) into missing values that are then dropped. The contract matches this only if the runner's 'as numbers' conversion also treats non-numeric strings as missing rather than raising.

Offense matching is case-sensitive in the script (pandas dict .map, 01_fetch_buffalo.py:182), so each rule sets case_sensitive=true and lists the mixed-case duplicate labels (Homicide, Sexual Assault, Robbery, Assault, Breaking & Entering, Theft, Theft of Vehicle) explicitly. None of those mixed-case labels appear in raw_cache.parquet (13 distinct incident_type_primary values in evidence/raw_cache_profile.json), and case-insensitive matching would give the same 90,467 mapped rows on this cache.

Output columns: the script renames police_district to district, council_district to beat, incident_type_primary to offense_raw, and writes an incident_id = str(case_number) plus address_1, zip_code, neighborhood, parent_incident_type (01_fetch_buffalo.py:203, 225-235). The contract carries only id, year, offense, coordinates and block group; these renames and passthrough columns are not expressed.
The script also writes offense_mapping.csv and README.md and prints summary tables (01_fetch_buffalo.py:241-254); these are side outputs, not row logic.
notes: Translation of evidence/01_fetch_buffalo.py. Rows kept: offense mapping is the OFFENSE_MAPPING dict (01_fetch_buffalo.py:82-132, identical to evidence/offense_mapping.csv, 18 labels); unlisted labels (CRIM NEGLIGENT HOMICIDE, SEXUAL ABUSE, Other Sexual Offense, THEFT OF SERVICES) fall through and are dropped as in the script. Coordinates: rows with missing/non-numeric lat or lon or at (0,0) dropped (lines 189-193). Year: derived from incident_datetime, kept 2018-2024 (lines 196-199); values are ISO strings like '2020-01-01T00:00:00.000' (raw_cache_profile.json), so date_format 'auto'; no year column exists in the pull, so year_field is empty. Id: case_number as string (line 203), de-duplicated keep-first (lines 205, 219). Live pull: Socrata $select of FIELDS (lines 70-74), $where on incident_datetime with exclusive end (line 137, rewritten with {start}/{end}), $order=case_number, $limit=50000 (lines 140-147). Block-group join: New York (FIPS 36) TIGER 2020 block groups, predicate within (lines 209-217). Recomputed on raw_cache.parquet with pandas replicating the script: 92,274 raw rows; 90,467 after the offense map (also the sum of the 10 mapped labels' counts in raw_cache_profile.json: 41,364+18,074+13,951+11,415+4,465+804+363+18+11+2); 86,438 after dropping 4,029 rows without usable coordinates (0 at (0,0)); 0 rows outside 2018-2024 (incident_datetime range 2018-01-01T00:00:00.000 to 2024-12-31T22:44:56.000); 0 duplicate case_numbers. By year 15,073 / 13,263 / 11,463 / 10,823 / 9,824 / 13,076 / 12,916 for 2018-2024, matching README.md lines 122-129 (total 86,438) and the 4,029 dropped rows at README.md line 150. Jurisdiction: the publisher is the Buffalo Police Department, a city PD (README.md lines 3-8), so jurisdiction_ids is Buffalo city only (36:municipal:place:3611000, 86,099 incidents in evidence/jurisdictions.csv row 2). The other 17 rows of jurisdictions.csv (rows 3-19: 16 Erie County municipalities plus the New York nonmunicipal remainder) sum to 342 incidents (151+57+31+31+16+15+15+6+4+3+3+2+2+2+2+1+1, summed from the incidents_2018_2024 column); the file total is 86,441, 3 more than the 86,438 kept rows, and the packet does not record why (the file lists both villages and the towns containing them, e.g. Kenmore village and Tonawanda town, so a point counted in both would explain an excess, but that is not shown in the evidence). These 342 are points outside the city limits under the source's 3-decimal rounding or geocoding (largest Cheektowaga town, 151, adjacent to the city; Angola village, 16), not additional BPD coverage. Live-pull note: 33 raw rows are dated 2024-12-31 (recomputed from raw_cache.parquet, first 10 characters of incident_datetime), so {end} must bind to the exclusive 2025-01-01 as in the script's line 137 for a live pull to keep them. exclusions_stated_by_publisher is empty: the evidence records no publisher-stated row exclusions, only publisher caveats (pre-2009 data flagged unreliable, README.md line 9; data described as preliminary, README.md lines 14-17). The offense exclusions above are the ingestion's decisions, not the publisher's.
